Help — using KASTR
Getting started
  1. Open KASTR — the app, or the web address you were given.
  2. Type your name and the access code you were given, then press Join. You start in the room you used last — the first time, in the Lobby.
  3. You arrive with your camera and microphone off. Turn them on with Camera and Mic at the top.
  4. The red button on the right leaves the room.
The screen
  • Toolbar: People (who is here), View (gallery or one big picture), Chat, More (record, room info, your profile, deafen, this help), Camera, Mic, Share, Leave. The small arrows beside Camera and Mic choose the device and effects.
  • Rooms list on the left (the arrow tab on its edge opens and closes it; on a phone, the tab at the left edge of the screen): every room on this relay, who is in it, and how long it has been going.
  • Room settings… (right-click a room; its creator or an admin): lock it or change its code, keep it open, rename it (everyone in it moves along), put it in a group, or Lock the view so only the creator or an admin can spotlight, pin or arrange for everyone.
  • Stage: the gallery shows everyone at the same size; speaker view shows one source big with the others in a strip beside it (underneath on a phone).
  • The Relay button at the top right shows whether the relay is healthy. The chevron next to it hides the top bar; the thin strip at the top brings it back.
Watching
  • Click or tap a tile to put it on your stage — only for you. View ▸ Gallery goes back to everyone.
  • A tile’s ⋯ menu (or right-click): Pin for me keeps it on your stage (several pins share it), Spotlight for everyone puts it on everybody’s stage, Remove spotlight takes it off again.
  • Pin to this room (same menu) lists a feed in the room for everyone — one from another room too — until someone unpins it. Spotlights and pins stay with the room when everyone leaves.
  • View ▸ Spotlight returns to what the room spotlighted. Focus on content downloads only the stage — useful on a slow connection.
  • Full screen: the tile’s full-screen button or F. Fill window: W. Esc leaves either.
  • Camera grids show several cameras in one tile; click a camera in a grid to open it at full quality.
  • Back to spotlight (top-left of the stage, or S) returns to what the room spotlighted, from the gallery or anything you opened.
  • Several things spotlit share the stage: drag one onto another to swap their places — everyone in the room sees the new order.
  • My room (More ▸ My room…) is a room only you see: pin feeds from any room into it (Pin to My room in a tile’s menu), spotlight and arrange them. It is kept on the hub under your name and a passcode (personal code), so it opens on any device; it is the first card in your rooms list. An admin can reset a forgotten code.
  • Share My room (right-click its card): give people access (they see <your name>’s room in their rooms list) or copy an invite link. Guests watch what you arrange and talk; only you arrange it, unless you tick Can arrange for one person. Guests are let in only while you are in My room — when you leave, everyone goes to the Lobby.
  • Right-click a person (the rooms list or People) ▸ Invite to the room you are in, or to My room: they get a prompt to Join or Ignore.
  • More ▸ Build a grid… makes a grid of cameras from any room you can see (rooms you watch too): drag cameras onto spots, several on one spot take turns on motion or on time. It is yours on this device, or Share with this room puts it on the room for everyone. Its ⋯ menu edits, renames or deletes it.
  • A coloured ring around someone means you are hearing them; a mic with a line through it means they are muted; an eye means they only watch.
Talking
  • Mic mutes and unmutes you. Its arrow picks the microphone and noise suppression.
  • Deafen (More ▸ Deafen, or D) turns off all sound from the room and mutes your mic. Others see that you are deafened.
  • To quieten one person for yourself, use Mute participant in their tile’s ⋯ menu (only you stop hearing them); Streams and volume in People sets each one’s level.
Sharing
  • Share ▸ a screen, a window or a browser tab; or an IP camera (RTSP), a camera on this computer, a media file, or an RTMP feed (for example a GoPro).
  • Several cameras can share one tile: Put in a grid… on a camera’s row.
  • Stop a share from the Share menu or the share’s own tile.
  • People ▸ Share invite copies a link that opens this room for 1 hour, 24 hours or 7 days — the person joining needs no access code or room code (it opens the KASTR app when they have it, else this host’s web page). The room’s creator or an admin revokes links in Room settings.
Rooms
  • The Lobby is where you wait: nothing is shared there and nobody sees who else is waiting. Pick a room on the stage or in the list to join it.
  • Switch rooms by clicking another room in the list (your mic is muted and camera turned off on the way).
  • Create a room with the ⊕ in the list’s header. A room can have its own code (locked) and can be kept open when empty.
  • Watch another room without leaving yours: the eye on its card, or right-click it ▸ Watch from …. Watched rooms stay silent until you choose Hear ….
Phones and tablets
  • Held upright, the stage is on top and everyone else is in a row underneath — swipe the row and tap someone to put them on the stage.
  • Full-screen app on an iPhone or iPad: open the page in Safari (not inside Teams or Outlook), tap Share ▸ Add to Home Screen and leave Open as Web App on.
  • On Android: Chrome’s menu ▸ Add to home screen (or Install app).
Keyboard shortcuts
← →the previous / next stream
1–9a stream by its number
Ggallery ↔ speaker view
Sback to the spotlight (from the gallery or anything else)
Ffull screen
Wfill the window
Mmute everything you hear
Ddeafen (again to undo)
PgUp PgDnmore people in the strip
Escclose panels; leave full screen
Something not working?
  • A tile that says connecting… or waiting on relay… is still reaching that person’s relay; it usually clears by itself within seconds.
  • Check the Relay button’s light (green is good) and More ▸ Room info.
  • Your administrator can collect every machine’s logs from the hub’s Relay page — say roughly when it happened.

Machines

Relays, hubs and camera boxes whose owner ticked Let fleet admins control this machine without asking on that machine’s own Relay page. Control opens its desktop in a private window with control already granted — it is never shown in any room; the machine shows a red bar with your name, anyone there can stop it, and every session is logged on the machine and on the hub.
